summary: A gi-focused companion to Octopus With Pajamas, organized around its half-guard, closed-guard and reverse-half sweep and back-take entries.
description: Compare the entry positions in Eduardo Telles’s published Octopus With Pajamas outline.
overview: This single-volume course offers several ways into the octopus theme. Half guard, closed guard and reverse half are separate study choices; their appearance in one syllabus does not make them a prescribed chain.

guide.display_title: Eduardo Telles: Octopus Guard in the Gi

fits: You want gi octopus material with an explicitly listed sleeve entry and several starting guards.
consider_alternative_if: For a no-gi syllabus with more headlock-response and turtle sections, compare Craig Jones’s Octopus Guard 2.0.

includes: Half-guard sweeps and back takes, butterfly variations, and closed-guard sleeve material.
Later sections name counters to octopus and reverse-half options.
limits: This single-volume gi survey covers several entries and counters; it offers less separately indexed headlock and turtle material than Craig Jones’s four-volume course.

start_here.title: Separate the starting guards
start_here.task: Use the free outline to make three headings: half guard, closed guard and reverse half. Place one sweep or back-take chapter beneath each. Choose the heading closest to a position you already study; if you have course access, begin with the half-guard sweep and compare the next elbow-post lesson without assuming what changes.

flashcards.question: Can a sleeve-dependent octopus entry be copied unchanged into no-gi?
flashcards.answer: No. The sleeve connection requires a gi; the published Telles outline explicitly includes a closed-guard sleeve entry.
flashcards.answer_line: No: the sleeve grip requires a gi.
